newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MOTORCYCLING-MALAYSIA STAY ON GRAND PRIX CIRCUIT.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-MALAYSIA STAY ON GRAND PRIX CIRCUIT.

text.p: Malaysia will host the opening round of the world motorcycle championship in April after settling differences with the series organisers.

The Automobile Association of Malaysia (AAM) signed a contract with grand prix organisers Dorna on Thursday confirming that it would be the local promoter and organiser for the race in the country until 2001.
AAM general manager Khir Anuar Mohamed said the deal guaranteed that this year's race would be held as scheduled at the Shah Alam circuit outside Kuala Lumpur on April 13.
Malaysia has been staging a grand prix since 1991 through the Selangor state government, which owns the track.

But the Selangor government's five-year contract with Dorna expired last year and it refused to renew the agreement this year, saying it might reconsider in 1999. Dorna then issued an ultimatum that Malaysia hold the race again this year or risk losing it in the future.
Khir Anuar said AAM had to take over from the Selangor government as Malaysia could not afford to lose the prestigious grand prix and the tourism potential that it offered.
